activities.anchor: Ionising radiation damages every cell it passes through
activities.caption: walk the distribution decision
activities.name: rtParadoxBranch

config.root: Ionising radiation damages every cell alike — tumour or healthy. The cure is a distribution problem, not a different substance.

choices.label: Stack it where the tumour is; spread it thin everywhere else
choices.feedback: The field's founding insight: dose distribution, plus biology, is what separates therapy from damage.

choices.label: Deliver the smallest useful dose, as a diagnostic X-ray does
choices.feedback: Diagnosis minimises dose; therapy deliberately delivers thousands of times more — and gets away with it only through geometry, timing and verification.

timing.text: One decision left: all at once, or divided in time?

choices.label: Divide it into recoverable daily pieces
choices.feedback: The schedule becomes part of the physics: time is the one step that is biology rather than engineering.

choices.label: Deliver everything in a single session
choices.feedback: The supporting biology is squandered — the schedule is a designed part of the dose, not an administrative detail.

end.text: Geometry, timing, verification — the three supports under the whole trick.

config.why: The beam cannot be seen, felt or taken back; every number on the console is an output of the physics, verified before the beam is turned on.

activities.anchor: What happens next defines the machine's two modes
activities.caption: rebuild the beam's journey, stage by stage
activities.name: rtBeamOrder

config.prompt: The linac is a chain of specialists — put the stages in beam order:
items: the electron gun injects electrons into the guide
standing-wave microwave fields surf them to near light speed
a bending magnet sweeps the beam around a corner, filtering by energy
the tungsten target converts their kinetic energy into X-ray photons
a flattening filter evens the forward-peaked beam
jaws set the rectangular field; the multileaf collimator sculpts it, moving live
config.why: Each stage hands a more refined beam to the next. For electron therapy the target is retracted so the electron beam itself exits — useful for shallow targets.

activities.caption: file each fact under the right machine
activities.name: rtCobaltSort

config.prompt: Two machines, two habits — file each fact:

items.label: gamma-emitting source that never switches off
must be shielded around the clock

config.why: That property shapes everything from machine servicing to decommissioning — the beam is manufactured on demand.

activities.anchor: The three physical rules underneath every calculation
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the three behaviours
activities.name: rtRulesCloze

config.text: Dose %%0%% exponentially with depth as photons are absorbed and scattered; it falls with the %%1%% square of distance from the source — double the distance, quarter the dose rate — and it builds up below the surface before it decays.
config.hint: First word: what the beam does with depth. Second: the geometric law that makes every 5 cm of patient geometry matter.

activities.caption: place d_max on the depth scale
activities.name: rtDmaxPlace

config.prompt: Depth in water, centimetres: a 6 MV beam peaks at about 1.5 cm. Where does a 10 MV beam peak?
config.why: About 2.5 cm at 10 MV, deeper still at higher energies — higher energies push the peak deeper and attenuate less, better for deep targets and worse for shallow ones.

activities.anchor: a more powerful machine — higher energy — is always
activities.caption: find the faulty line — an energy briefing
activities.name: rtEnergySpot

config.prompt: One line of this machine-room briefing is wrong — click it:
lines: Higher energies push d_max deeper and attenuate less — better for deep targets.
Lower energies keep dose more contained near the entrance — kinder en route to a shallow target.
Higher energy is always the better machine.
6 MV machines treat the great majority of cases.
config.correction: Energy is a matching decision, not a ranking — pushed deeper, the peak can worsen the dose to healthy tissue on the way to a shallow target.
config.why: The best beam is the one whose depth–dose curve fits the patient's geometry.

activities.anchor: The multileaf collimator's precision is recent history
activities.caption: drag the divider — blocks versus leaves
activities.name: rtShapingCompare

config.prompt: Field shaping, then and now — drag the divider.

before.label: Custom blocks
before.text: Dense alloy cast to the tumour's projected shape, wedged into the beam for each treatment — hours per patient, one static shape per field, daily handling.

after.label: Multileaf collimator
after.text: Motorised tungsten leaves moving during treatment — dozens of changing field shapes paint an intensity pattern no static block could, in minutes of automated delivery.

config.why: The clinical payoff: tumour concavities dosed while a nearby organ is protected. Every mechanical refinement of the beam buys normal tissue a smaller dose.

activities.caption: true or false — the modern layers
activities.name: rtModernJudge

statements.s: IMRT/VMAT uses the moving leaves to vary dose rate across the field hundreds of times per beam.
statements.why: Carving high dose around organs-at-risk with concavities no single field could produce.

statements.s: IGRT adds daily on-board imaging because targets move with breathing and patients change day to day.
Flattening-filter-free beams trade very high dose rates for beam uniformity.
statements.why: The other way round: they trade beam uniformity FOR very high dose rates — which is what makes stereotactic sessions short enough to hold still.

statements.s: Each modern layer is the same linac with a sharper question asked of it.
statements.why: IMRT, IGRT and flattening-filter-free delivery are refinements of one machine, not separate technologies.
